es: Reconocer expresiones de probabilidad (definitely, highly likely, probably, unlikely, a slim chance, no chance), ordenarlas por fuerza y ligarlas al nivel de riesgo de un aviso.

teaching.en: The forecast says snow will definitely reach the higher villages by midnight, so the authorities will issue a warning for every driver on the coast road.
teaching.es: El pronóstico dice que la nieve llegará sin duda a los pueblos más altos antes de medianoche, así que las autoridades emitirán un aviso para todos los conductores de la carretera de la costa.
teaching.explanationEs: Will definitely + verbo: certeza casi total; el adverbio va después de will. Issue a warning = emitir un aviso oficial.
segments: The forecast says snow will definitely reach the higher villages by midnight, so
the authorities will issue a warning for every driver on the coast road.
teaching.audioText: The forecast says snow will definitely reach the higher villages by midnight, so the authorities will issue a warning for every driver on the coast road.

teaching.en: A late frost is highly likely to damage the crops this week, which is why the farmers are already taking precautions.
teaching.es: Es muy probable que una helada tardía dañe los cultivos esta semana, por eso los agricultores ya están tomando precauciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Highly likely: probabilidad alta. Likely es un adjetivo, así que se dice is likely to + verbo.
segments: A late frost is highly likely to damage the crops this
week, which is why the farmers are already taking precautions.
teaching.audioText: A late frost is highly likely to damage the crops this week, which is why the farmers are already taking precautions.

teaching.en: We will probably reach the refuge before dark, and there is a fair chance of a clear sunset, but with this wind I would not rule out a late start.
teaching.es: Probablemente llegaremos al refugio antes de que oscurezca y hay una posibilidad razonable de un atardecer despejado, pero con este viento no descartaría una salida tardía.
teaching.explanationEs: A fair chance: probabilidad razonable, más que remota. Rule out es un verbo frasal: descartar; would not rule out suaviza: «no descartaría».
segments: We will probably reach the refuge before dark, and there is a fair chance of
a clear sunset, but with this wind I would not rule out a late start.
teaching.audioText: We will probably reach the refuge before dark, and there is a fair chance of a clear sunset, but with this wind I would not rule out a late start.

teaching.en: Heavy rain is unlikely before noon, although a sudden thunderstorm remains a distinct possibility once the valley warms up.
teaching.es: Es poco probable que llueva con fuerza antes del mediodía, aunque una tormenta repentina sigue siendo una posibilidad real cuando el valle se caliente.
teaching.explanationEs: Unlikely = poco probable. A distinct possibility: no es seguro, pero hay que tomarlo en serio.
segments: Heavy rain is unlikely before noon, although a sudden thunderstorm
remains a distinct possibility once the valley warms up.
teaching.audioText: Heavy rain is unlikely before noon, although a sudden thunderstorm remains a distinct possibility once the valley warms up.

teaching.en: There is only a slim chance that the pass will reopen today, and it is unlikely that the station will have power before morning.
teaching.es: Solo hay una posibilidad escasa de que el paso reabra hoy, y es poco probable que la estación tenga electricidad antes de la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: A slim chance: baja pero no nula. No chance significa imposible.
segments: There is only a slim chance that the pass will reopen today,
and it is unlikely that the station will have power before morning.
teaching.audioText: There is only a slim chance that the pass will reopen today, and it is unlikely that the station will have power before morning.

teaching.en: A hazard is whatever can cause harm, whereas the risk is how probable that harm is: black ice is a constant hazard, yet the risk depends on the temperature.
teaching.es: Un peligro es aquello que puede causar daño, mientras que el riesgo es lo probable que sea ese daño: el hielo negro es un peligro constante, pero el riesgo depende de la temperatura.
teaching.explanationEs: Hazard nombra el peligro en sí; risk o chance miden su probabilidad. No son sinónimos.
segments: A hazard is whatever can cause harm, whereas the risk is how probable that harm
is: black ice is a constant hazard, yet the risk depends on the temperature.
teaching.audioText: A hazard is whatever can cause harm, whereas the risk is how probable that harm is: black ice is a constant hazard, yet the risk depends on the temperature.

prompt.es: Lee el parte: ¿qué da por casi seguro el pronóstico?

choices.text: The wind will drop before the last ferry leaves.
Clear skies will return tomorrow morning.
A storm will reach the harbour this evening.

feedback.es: Will definitely deja casi sin duda que ocurrirá; might solo abre una posibilidad y unlikely o slim chance la rebajan.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que no deja duda: no es might ni slim chance.

origin.text: Coastal forecast: a storm will definitely reach the harbour this evening, although the wind might drop a little before the last ferry leaves. Fog is unlikely, and there is only a slim chance of clear skies tomorrow morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es muy probable que una helada tardía dañe las cosechas.»

feedback.es: Highly likely + to + verbo expresa una probabilidad alta; likely es el adjetivo que admite to.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa «probable» y se escribe antes de to.

origin.text: Farmers are worried, because two cold, clear nights are forecast. A late frost is highly ___ to damage the crops.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No podemos descartar un retraso a causa de la niebla.»

answer.text: We cannot rule out a delay because of the fog

feedback.es: Rule out es un verbo frasal: descartar. Las dos palabras van juntas y el objeto va detrás.

hint.es: Rule y out van seguidos; después viene lo que se descarta.

prompt.es: Escucha el programa de radio y elige qué considera más probable la meteoróloga.

choices.text: Snow on the high ground.
A thunderstorm in the valley after dark.
A power cut in the mountain villages.

feedback.es: «All but certain» es lo más seguro de la escala: la nieve en altura. La tormenta es solo una posibilidad real y el corte de luz no se descarta.

origin.audio: On this morning's radio show, the forecaster was careful with her wording. She told listeners that snow on the high ground was all but certain, that rain in the valley was highly likely by the afternoon, and that a thunderstorm was still a distinct possibility after dark. Clear skies, she added, were unlikely before Sunday, and she would not rule out a short power cut in the mountain villages. Anyone planning a long drive north, she said, should decide by noon rather than hope for the best.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada aviso con el nivel de riesgo que expresa.

pairs: A flood is definitely on its way.
We cannot rule out a flood.
There is a distinct possibility of a flood.
A flood is highly unlikely.

feedback.es: Definitely marca certeza, rule out aparece en negativo como «no descartar», distinct possibility es posible y en serio y highly unlikely rebaja la probabilidad.

pairs: A flood is definitely on its way.
We cannot rule out a flood.
There is a distinct possibility of a flood.
A flood is highly unlikely.

prompt.es: Lee la nota: ¿qué actitud transmite la organizadora ante la excursión?

choices.text: Growing anxiety: she sees the weather as the main threat.
Measured confidence: she expects to go ahead but allows for a new route.
Mild anger: she thinks the media are exaggerating the forecast.

feedback.es: Dice que probablemente seguirán con el plan, pero no descarta cambiar de ruta: optimismo moderado; además señala que el peligro real es el cansancio, no el tiempo.

origin.text: Note from the organiser: Given the forecast, we will probably run the hike as planned, but I would not rule out a change of route. Thunderstorms are unlikely before four, so the real hazard is tiredness, not the weather.

prompt.es: Escucha la llamada: ¿cuándo quiere el guía que vuelvan los grupos?

choices.text: Before the morning is over.
After the snow has stopped.
Early in the afternoon.

feedback.es: El guía pide estar de vuelta en el refugio a la una, es decir, a primera hora de la tarde.

origin.audio: Mia, it's Leo at the mountain refuge. Listen, the guide has just posted the update: there is a slim chance of sun until nine, then cloud, and snow is highly likely after midday. He would not rule out heavy snow on the high ground, which is why he wants every group back at the refuge by one. If you leave at six, you will probably make it. If we set off at eight, I would not count on it.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué da a entender Leo sobre salir a las ocho?

choices.text: That a late start would be taking a real risk.
That the guide would not allow a late start.
That the snow will have cleared by then.

feedback.es: «I would not count on it» suaviza, pero deja claro que salir tarde probablemente no permitirá volver a tiempo: es una apuesta arriesgada.

origin.audio: Mia, it's Leo at the mountain refuge. Listen, the guide has just posted the update: there is a slim chance of sun until nine, then cloud, and snow is highly likely after midday. He would not rule out heavy snow on the high ground, which is why he wants every group back at the refuge by one. If you leave at six, you will probably make it. If we set off at eight, I would not count on it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Con aire cálido y nubes bajas, una tormenta repentina es una posibilidad real.»

feedback.es: A distinct (o real, strong) possibility significa que no es seguro, pero hay que contar con ello.

origin.text: The valley is warming fast. With low cloud building over the hills, a sudden storm is a ___ possibility.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es muy probable que la carretera esté cerrada por la tarde.»

answer.text: The road is highly likely to be closed by the afternoon

feedback.es: Highly likely + to + verbo expresa probabilidad alta; be closed es la pasiva del estado de la carretera.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué postura adopta el jefe de obra ante un cierre total?

choices.text: It is highly likely, and he expects the engineers to confirm it.
It is unlikely, but he keeps the option open.
It is unlikely, so he sees no reason to treat the warning seriously.

feedback.es: Dice que un cierre es poco probable pero se niega a descartarlo: lo mantiene como opción.

origin.audio: At the safety meeting, the site manager summed things up. The bridge will definitely be inspected on Friday, he said. A full closure is unlikely, but he refused to rule it out until the engineers report back. He added that nobody should treat the warning as routine, since the hazard had not changed, only the chances.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿con qué propósito da la naviera la cifra de una entre cinco?

choices.text: To reassure passengers that a cancellation is out of the question.
To warn passengers that a cancellation is more likely than not.
To explain why passengers should keep their plans flexible.

feedback.es: La cifra sirve para justificar el consejo: la probabilidad es baja, pero real, así que conviene un billete flexible.

origin.text: Subject: Ferry update. Dear passengers, our forecast team puts the chance of a cancellation at about one in five. That is low, but it is real, so we recommend a flexible ticket. The chances are that we will leave on time, and we will confirm by phone at noon.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las piedras sueltas son un peligro permanente; el riesgo depende de la lluvia.»

feedback.es: Hazard nombra la fuente de peligro; el riesgo añade cuán probable es el daño.

origin.text: Loose rocks above the path are a permanent ___, but the actual risk depends on how hard it rains.

title.es: En el caso poco probable de

es: Formular avisos de riesgo con in the unlikely event (of/that), the odds are, there's a slim chance y the worst-case scenario, eligiendo la estructura que sigue a cada expresión.

teaching.en: In the unlikely event of a fire, guests should leave the building by the nearest stairs and gather at the meeting point outside.
teaching.es: En el caso poco probable de un incendio, los huéspedes deben salir del edificio por las escaleras más cercanas y reunirse en el punto de encuentro exterior.
teaching.explanationEs: In the unlikely event of + nombre, + instrucción: el aviso formal de seguridad. La instrucción va en imperativo o con should.
segments: In the unlikely event of a fire, guests should leave the building
by the nearest stairs and gather at the meeting point outside.
teaching.audioText: In the unlikely event of a fire, guests should leave the building by the nearest stairs and gather at the meeting point outside.

teaching.en: In the unlikely event that the ferry is cancelled, all passengers will receive a full refund within ten working days.
teaching.es: En el caso poco probable de que se cancele el transbordador, todos los pasajeros recibirán un reembolso completo en un plazo de diez días laborables.
teaching.explanationEs: In the unlikely event that + oración completa; el resultado va con will o con un imperativo.
segments: In the unlikely event that the ferry is cancelled, all
passengers will receive a full refund within ten working days.
teaching.audioText: In the unlikely event that the ferry is cancelled, all passengers will receive a full refund within ten working days.

teaching.en: The odds are that the trail will be open by noon, so there is no need to change the plan just yet.
teaching.es: Lo más probable es que el sendero esté abierto al mediodía, así que no hace falta cambiar el plan todavía.
teaching.explanationEs: The odds are (that) + oración: probabilidad alta. Pese al español, no lleva subjuntivo.
segments: The odds are that the trail will be open by noon,
so there is no need to change the plan just yet.
teaching.audioText: The odds are that the trail will be open by noon, so there is no need to change the plan just yet.

teaching.en: There is a slim chance that the guide will have to evacuate the camp, which is why every group carries a contingency plan.
teaching.es: Hay una posibilidad escasa de que el guía tenga que evacuar el campamento, por eso cada grupo lleva un plan de contingencia.
teaching.explanationEs: There's a slim chance (that) + oración: probabilidad baja. Un contingency plan es el plan B para cuando algo sale mal.
segments: There is a slim chance that the guide will have to evacuate
the camp, which is why every group carries a contingency plan.
teaching.audioText: There is a slim chance that the guide will have to evacuate the camp, which is why every group carries a contingency plan.

teaching.en: The worst-case scenario is that the river could flood overnight and we would have to turn back, so it pays to brace for delays.
teaching.es: En el peor de los casos, el río podría desbordarse durante la noche y tendríamos que dar la vuelta, así que conviene prepararse para los retrasos.
teaching.explanationEs: The worst-case scenario is (that) + oración: nombra lo peor que podría pasar. Brace for + nombre: prepararse para algo difícil.
segments: The worst-case scenario is that the river could flood overnight and we
would have to turn back, so it pays to brace for delays.
teaching.audioText: The worst-case scenario is that the river could flood overnight and we would have to turn back, so it pays to brace for delays.

teaching.en: In an emergency a calm leader makes all the difference: if anyone feels dizzy, sit them down and call for help straight away.
teaching.es: En una emergencia, un líder tranquilo marca la diferencia: si alguien se marea, siéntalo y pide ayuda de inmediato.
teaching.explanationEs: Emergency es la situación grave e inesperada; dizzy describe a quien siente que todo da vueltas.
segments: In an emergency a calm leader makes all the difference: if anyone
feels dizzy, sit them down and call for help straight away.
teaching.audioText: In an emergency a calm leader makes all the difference: if anyone feels dizzy, sit them down and call for help straight away.

prompt.es: Completa: «En el caso poco probable de que se cancele el vuelo, recibirá un reembolso.»

feedback.es: Tras event, una oración completa se introduce con that; of se reserva para un nombre.

hint.es: Es el conector que introduce una oración completa tras event.

origin.text: The airline has apologised for the disruption. In the unlikely event ___ the flight is cancelled, passengers will receive a full refund.

prompt.es: Elige la versión correcta de la instrucción para un corte de luz.

choices.text: In the unlikely event of a power cut, use the stairs.
In the unlikely event of a power cut is, use the stairs.
In the unlikely event that a power cut, use the stairs.

feedback.es: Event of + nombre (a power cut) es correcto; las otras dos mezclan of con un verbo o that con un nombre sin verbo.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que sigue a event of: solo un nombre, sin verbo conjugado.

origin.text: Hotel notice: the lifts are checked every month, and the emergency lights come on at once. Please read the instruction for a power cut.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay una posibilidad escasa de que el guía tenga que evacuar el campamento.»

answer.text: There's a slim chance that the guide will have to evacuate the camp

feedback.es: There's a slim chance that + oración con will expresa una probabilidad baja sobre el futuro.

hint.es: Empieza con There's y deja la oración completa tras that.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué podría pasar si sube el viento.

choices.text: The ship would return to the harbour at once.
Passengers could be asked to remain indoors.
Everybody would be moved to another ship.

feedback.es: El aviso dice que hay una posibilidad escasa de que suba el viento y que la tripulación podría pedir a los pasajeros que se queden dentro.

origin.audio: Good evening, and welcome on board. Before we leave the harbour, a few words on safety. The odds are that the crossing will be smooth, since the sea is calm and the forecast is good. There is a slim chance that the wind will rise after midnight, in which case the crew may ask passengers to stay inside. In the unlikely event that we have to evacuate the ship, please do not use the lifts: walk calmly to the nearest exit and wait for instructions from the crew.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada aviso con su traducción.

pairs: The odds are that the concert will go ahead.

pairs.es: Lo más probable es que el concierto siga adelante.

pairs: In the unlikely event that it rains, we will move inside.

pairs.es: En el caso poco probable de que llueva, nos pasaremos al interior.

pairs: The worst-case scenario is that we lose a day.

pairs.es: En el peor de los casos, perdemos un día.

feedback.es: The odds are that expresa probabilidad alta, event that abre un caso improbable con oración completa y worst-case scenario nombra lo peor.

pairs.es: Lo más probable es que el concierto siga adelante.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje: ¿qué actitud transmite la organizadora ante el riesgo?

choices.text: Doubt: she says nobody can tell whether the match will go ahead.
Mild alarm: she thinks the pitch will probably flood tonight.
Calm: she expects the match to go ahead and has a plan B.

feedback.es: Dice que lo probable es que se juegue y prepara una llamada de aviso: tranquilidad con un plan de reserva.

origin.text: Dear volunteers, the odds are that Saturday's match will go ahead, but there is a slim chance that the pitch will flood after tonight's rain. In the unlikely event that we have to cancel, I will phone everyone by eight. The worst-case scenario is a lost day, not a disaster.

prompt.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué se promete si cancelan el último tren.

choices.text: A free ride home.
A night at a nearby hotel.
A refund of the ticket price.

feedback.es: El aviso promete un taxi a casa sin coste si el tren se cancela; el hotel y el reembolso no se mencionan.

origin.audio: Attention, passengers on the night train. There's a slim chance that the last connection will be cancelled tonight because of the snow. The odds are that it will run, but a little late. In the unlikely event that it is cancelled, a taxi will take you home at no charge, so nobody will be left waiting on the platform.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿con qué fin menciona el aviso el taxi?

choices.text: To persuade travellers to choose a taxi instead of the train.
To reassure travellers that they will not be left stranded.
To warn travellers that the train will probably be cancelled.

feedback.es: El taxi se ofrece como red de seguridad: tranquiliza a quien temiera quedarse sin viaje, sin afirmar que el tren se cancele.

origin.audio: Attention, passengers on the night train. There's a slim chance that the last connection will be cancelled tonight because of the snow. The odds are that it will run, but a little late. In the unlikely event that it is cancelled, a taxi will take you home at no charge, so nobody will be left waiting on the platform.

prompt.es: Completa: «Incluso en el peor de los casos, podemos pasar la noche en el refugio.»

feedback.es: Worst-case scenario nombra lo peor que podría pasar; tras in the va el sustantivo, y even marca que aun así hay solución.

origin.text: We have checked the route twice. Even in the worst-case ___, we can spend the night at the refuge.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En el caso poco probable de que te marees, siéntate.»

answer.text: In the unlikely event that you feel dizzy, sit down

feedback.es: Event that introduce una oración completa (you feel dizzy) y la instrucción va en imperativo.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender la directora al pedir un plan de contingencia?

choices.text: That the forecast cannot be trusted at all.
That the festival will be cancelled if the storm arrives.
That preparing matters even when the risk is small.

feedback.es: Pide prepararse aunque lo probable sea buen tiempo: lo improbable pero grave justifica tener un plan B.

origin.audio: At the planning meeting, the festival director was honest. The odds are that the weather will hold, she said, but she refused to treat the forecast as a promise. She asked each team to prepare a contingency plan, because in the unlikely event that the storm arrives early, nobody will have time to decide what to do.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿por qué incluye el hotel esta cláusula?

choices.text: To reassure guests that their money is hardly at risk.
To warn guests that snow will very likely close the road.
To tell guests that refunds are only paid after the weekend.

feedback.es: La cláusula ofrece cambiar la fecha o devolver el dinero, así que reduce el riesgo de reservar; no anuncia nieve segura.

origin.text: Dear guest, thank you for booking the mountain weekend. The odds are that the roads will stay clear, but a forecast is not a guarantee. In the unlikely event that snow closes the road, we will move your stay to another weekend or give you a full refund, as you prefer.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si el río sigue creciendo, los guías tendrán que evacuar el campamento.»

feedback.es: Evacuate es sacar a todos de un lugar peligroso; va seguido directamente del lugar.

origin.text: The river has been rising since dawn. If it keeps rising, the guides will have to ___ the camp before dark.

es: Comprender un parte de montaña: localizar el peligro, su grado de certeza (will, are expected, may), el momento y la urgencia de la acción recomendada.

teaching.en: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge from mid-morning, so the exposed sections of the path will be hard to cross.
teaching.es: Se esperan ráfagas de sesenta kilómetros por hora por encima de la cresta desde media mañana, así que los tramos expuestos del sendero serán difíciles de cruzar.
teaching.explanationEs: Are expected: el parte anuncia el peligro con voz pasiva. Busca el fenómeno, la cifra y el lugar. Exposed = sin protección del viento.
segments: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge from mid-morning,
so the exposed sections of the path will be hard to cross.
teaching.audioText: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge from mid-morning, so the exposed sections of the path will be hard to cross.

teaching.en: Visibility will drop sharply in cloud after noon, and conditions are likely to deteriorate further as the cold front moves in.
teaching.es: La visibilidad caerá bruscamente entre nubes después del mediodía y es probable que las condiciones empeoren aún más cuando llegue el frente frío.
teaching.explanationEs: Will drop: previsto casi con seguridad; sharply indica un cambio rápido. Are likely to deteriorate: empeoramiento probable.
segments: Visibility will drop sharply in cloud after noon, and conditions are
likely to deteriorate further as the cold front moves in.
teaching.audioText: Visibility will drop sharply in cloud after noon, and conditions are likely to deteriorate further as the cold front moves in.

teaching.en: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers who are still high up should take shelter in the nearest refuge rather than push on.
teaching.es: Son posibles tormentas eléctricas a media tarde, así que los excursionistas que sigan en lo alto deberían refugiarse en el refugio más cercano en lugar de seguir adelante.
teaching.explanationEs: Are possible: no es seguro. Take shelter = refugiarse. Should + verbo: consejo con urgencia media.
segments: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers who are still high up
should take shelter in the nearest refuge rather than push on.
teaching.audioText: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers who are still high up should take shelter in the nearest refuge rather than push on.

teaching.en: Temperatures will fall below freezing overnight, so the descent may be slippery once the sun goes down and the path starts to ice over.
teaching.es: Las temperaturas bajarán de cero durante la noche, así que el descenso podría ser resbaladizo cuando se ponga el sol y el sendero empiece a helarse.
teaching.explanationEs: Below freezing = por debajo de cero (sin of). May marca un riesgo posible, no seguro.
segments: Temperatures will fall below freezing overnight, so the descent may be slippery
once the sun goes down and the path starts to ice over.
teaching.audioText: Temperatures will fall below freezing overnight, so the descent may be slippery once the sun goes down and the path starts to ice over.

teaching.en: The mountain bulletin is updated at six and again at noon, so anyone planning a long day should read the latest version before setting off.
teaching.es: El parte de montaña se actualiza a las seis y de nuevo al mediodía, así que quien planee una jornada larga debería leer la última versión antes de salir.
teaching.explanationEs: Bulletin: el parte oficial. Before + -ing: antes de hacer algo, sin sujeto repetido.
segments: The mountain bulletin is updated at six and again at noon, so anyone
planning a long day should read the latest version before setting off.
teaching.audioText: The mountain bulletin is updated at six and again at noon, so anyone planning a long day should read the latest version before setting off.

teaching.en: Treat this as a serious alert: if the wind increases or the cloud comes down, turn back at once rather than hope it will pass.
teaching.es: Tómalo como una alerta seria: si aumenta el viento o bajan las nubes, da la vuelta de inmediato en lugar de esperar a que pase.
teaching.explanationEs: Serious y at once elevan la urgencia: hay que actuar ya. Rather than + verbo base: en lugar de.
segments: Treat this as a serious alert: if the wind increases or the cloud
comes down, turn back at once rather than hope it will pass.
teaching.audioText: Treat this as a serious alert: if the wind increases or the cloud comes down, turn back at once rather than hope it will pass.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué peligro anuncia el parte para la zona alta.

choices.text: Thick fog that lasts all day.
Strong wind from mid-morning.
Thunderstorms in the valley from ten.

feedback.es: Gusts son ráfagas de viento y el parte las sitúa en la zona alta desde las diez; la niebla llega hacia el mediodía y no se habla de tormentas.

hint.es: Piensa qué son las ráfagas y desde qué hora se esperan.

origin.audio: Mountain bulletin issued at seven. Gusts of seventy kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge from ten o'clock. Visibility will drop sharply in cloud by midday, and anyone planning the exposed crossing should think again.

prompt.es: Lee el parte y elige cuánta certeza tiene sobre las tormentas.

choices.text: They are certain to arrive before two.
They are impossible on the ridge today.
They are possible, but not certain.

feedback.es: Are possible indica que pueden ocurrir, pero no lo afirma; will habría marcado certeza.

hint.es: Observa si el parte usa will o una expresión de posibilidad.

origin.text: Bulletin: a cold front will reach the ridge by midday. Thunderstorms are possible after two o'clock, although the heaviest rain is expected near the coast. Anyone still on the summit by then should start down at once.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las condiciones empeorarán cuando llegue el frente.»

feedback.es: Deteriorate significa empeorar poco a poco; es el verbo habitual para hablar de las condiciones del tiempo.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «empeorar» y acompaña a conditions.

origin.text: The morning will stay bright and calm. After that, conditions are likely to ___ as the front moves in.

prompt.es: Escucha el parte y elige qué se aconseja a quien siga arriba a las dos.

choices.text: To take shelter rather than keep climbing.
To press on to the summit while the cloud is still high.
To wait on the ridge until the thunderstorms have passed.

feedback.es: El parte dice que quien siga arriba a las dos debe refugiarse en lugar de continuar; el hielo llega de noche y las tormentas son solo posibles.

origin.audio: Mountain bulletin for Saturday. A cold front will reach the ridge by midday, and gusts of eighty kilometres an hour are expected on the exposed sections. Visibility will drop sharply in cloud from about one o'clock, and thunderstorms are possible between three and five. Temperatures will fall below freezing after dark, so the descent may be slippery. Conditions are likely to deteriorate quickly in the afternoon, and anyone still on the high ground by two should take shelter rather than try to continue. Treat this as a serious alert.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada señal del parte con su certeza o urgencia.

pairs: Gusts of eighty are expected on the ridge.
Thunderstorms may develop after three.
Take shelter at once if the cloud comes down.
Conditions will improve gradually over the week.

feedback.es: Are expected señala algo previsto, may algo posible, at once urgencia alta y gradually un cambio lento.

pairs: Gusts of eighty are expected on the ridge.
Thunderstorms may develop after three.
Take shelter at once if the cloud comes down.

prompt.es: Lee la nota del guía: ¿qué postura refleja ante la salida?

choices.text: Nervous doubt: he would cancel if the group agreed to it.
Firm care: a fixed turn-back time despite the good start.
Easy confidence: the fine morning means the warning can wait.

feedback.es: Acepta salir porque la mañana es buena, pero fija una hora límite sin excepciones: cautela firme.

origin.text: Guide's note to the group: the morning looks fine and the wind is light, so I am happy to set off. However, the bulletin warns that conditions are likely to deteriorate after two. We start at six, and anyone who is not off the ridge by one turns back with me. No exceptions.

prompt.es: Escucha el parte y elige por qué ruta deben bajar los excursionistas.

choices.text: Along the ridge, but only as far as the refuge.
By the forest road on the far side.
By the lower path through the valley.

feedback.es: El coordinador pide bajar por el camino del valle y no por la cresta expuesta, porque el descenso está resbaladizo.

origin.audio: On the midday radio show, the mountain rescue coordinator read out the latest bulletin. The wind is already very strong on the ridge, he said, and visibility is poor above two thousand metres. Thunderstorms are expected by four, although they may arrive earlier. He asked hikers to come down by the valley path, not along the exposed ridge, because the descent is slippery after the rain. He stressed that this was only a warning, not a reason to panic.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud pide el coordinador a los excursionistas?

choices.text: Care, but without alarm.
Alarm: leave the mountain at once by any route.
Calm: a warning of this kind can safely be ignored.

feedback.es: Al decir «only a warning, not a reason to panic» pide cautela sin alarmismo: bajar con cuidado, ni entrar en pánico ni restar importancia.

origin.audio: On the midday radio show, the mountain rescue coordinator read out the latest bulletin. feedback.es: Exposed describe un tramo sin protección frente al viento o al frío; sheltered es su contrario.

origin.text: The lower path is sheltered. Avoid the ___ sections of the ridge, where nothing protects you from the wind.

choices.text: The strength of the gusts on the ridge.
The loss of visibility in the afternoon.
The cold during the descent after dark.

feedback.es: Las ráfagas son «routine»; lo que le preocupa es que la visibilidad caiga después del mediodía, y por eso fija una hora límite.

origin.audio: At the refuge meeting, the head guide went through the bulletin line by line. Gusts were expected, he said, which was routine for the season. What worried him was the forecast of falling visibility after midday, because a group that cannot see the path can lose an hour in minutes. So the rule for tomorrow is simple: nobody starts the crossing after nine.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje: ¿qué da a entender el organizador?

choices.text: That the trip will go ahead unless a storm actually arrives.
That the ridge path will be avoided whatever the bulletin says.
That the decision depends on the morning bulletin.

feedback.es: La decisión se toma a las seis según el parte: si no ha mejorado, la excursión no sale; las tormentas solo son posibles, no seguras.

origin.text: To all members: the guide has posted an alert for tomorrow. Thunderstorms are possible, not certain, and the path along the ridge is exposed. I will make the final decision at six. If the bulletin has not improved by then, the trip will not go ahead, and I will call each of you myself.

feedback.es: Gusts son golpes bruscos de viento; en un tramo expuesto pueden desequilibrar a un excursionista.

teaching.en: A waterproof jacket is worth its weight in gold up here, so take precautions even if the morning looks bright and calm.

teaching.explanationEs: Take precautions = tomar medidas antes de que haya un problema. Even if + presente: aunque, sin will.

You may use the upper path, she said, provided that everyone stays together, and nobody goes outside the marked route unless I say so. Take a torch in case we come down late, and a waterproof jacket in case the clouds build up, even though the sky is blue now. And finally, you had better start drinking water early, because on a long climb it is too late to begin when you are already tired.

prompt.es: Escribe seis avisos de seguridad para una ruta de montaña.

answer.text: Safety notices for the ridge walk. 1. Do not start the climb unless the sky is clear at seven in the morning, because the route becomes hazardous when the rocks are wet. 2. You may walk along the ridge provided that the wind is light, and you may stop at the shelter as long as you leave no rubbish. 3. Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark. 4. Carry a waterproof jacket in case the afternoon storm arrives earlier than the forecast says. 5. You had better turn back if the path is icy, because a fall here is a real danger and help is hours away. 6. When in doubt, err on the side of caution: it is sensible to rest in the shelter and wait for the guide. Take precautions, and enjoy the walk.

Carry a waterproof jacket in case the afternoon storm arrives earlier than the forecast says. 5. You had better turn back if the path is icy, because a fall here is a real danger and help is hours away. 6. When in doubt, err on the side of caution: it is sensible to rest in the shelter and wait for the guide. Take precautions, and enjoy the walk.

Notice 1: Nobody should go up unless a guide has checked the path that morning, because the rocks can be very slippery. Notice 2: The shelter is open to everyone provided that you leave it clean and tidy. Notice 3: Bring a warm coat and a torch in case the night is cold or you finish late. Notice 4: You had better start early if you want to reach the summit before the clouds arrive. Notice 5: It is safe to cross the bridge as long as it is dry, but if you are not sure, err on the side of caution and use the lower path. Notice 6: Keep your phone charged in case you need help, and take precautions against the wind, since it can change very quickly on the ridge.

feedback.es: Un buen cartel une cada instrucción con una condición en presente: unless para excepciones, provided that o as long as para condiciones, in case para prevenir y had better para aconsejar con fuerza.

origin.text: Eres guía en un sendero que sube por un bosque y termina en una cresta. Escribe un cartel con seis avisos (entre 130 y 200 palabras). Usa unless, provided that o as long as, in case y had better, y nombra en cada aviso un peligro o una medida concreta.

title.en: Risk briefing for a mountain trip
title.es: Charla de riesgos para una excursión

es: Presentar en una charla breve los riesgos de una excursión (peligro, probabilidad, consecuencia y medida de prevención) y deducir las causas de un incidente con must have, might have y can't have.

teaching.en: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.
teaching.es: Esta charla tiene tres partes: el peligro, el riesgo y la medida preventiva que tomamos, y las repasaremos en ese orden.
teaching.explanationEs: Una charla de riesgos sigue un orden fijo: peligro, riesgo (probabilidad) y medida. Preventive measure = medida para evitar un problema.
segments: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive
measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.
teaching.audioText: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.

teaching.en: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.
teaching.es: Es probable que haya hielo en la cresta y la consecuencia podría ser una caída grave, así que los participantes deberían tratar cada paso como si importara.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de la probabilidad se nombra la consecuencia: could be + lo que podría pasar.
segments: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a
serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.
teaching.audioText: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.

teaching.en: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.
teaching.es: Para evitar una caída, todos los participantes deben revisar su equipo, porque una correa suelta suele ser la causa de fondo de un accidente.
teaching.explanationEs: To prevent + nombre abre la medida; must marca la obligación. Root cause: la causa de fondo, no el síntoma.
segments: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because
a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.
teaching.audioText: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.

teaching.en: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have happened then, and a hiker who slipped could easily sustain an injury.
teaching.es: El camino estaba mojado tras la lluvia, así que el incidente debe de haber ocurrido entonces, y un excursionista que resbalara podría sufrir fácilmente una lesión.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado, a partir de una prueba. Sustain an injury: sufrir una lesión.
segments: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have

teaching.audioText: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have happened then, and a hiker who slipped could easily sustain an injury.

teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: deducción negativa casi segura. In hindsight: valorar algo una vez que ya se sabe cómo acabó.
segments: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have

teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad sobre el pasado, sin seguridad. Near miss: un percance que pudo acabar mal y no lo hizo.
segments: The incident was only a near miss and might have started with a missed turn in

origin.audio: Good morning, and welcome to the briefing. I will cover the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure for each stage. The first hazard is the river crossing. Ice is unlikely today, but fast water could push a hiker off balance, and the consequence could be an injury or lost equipment. To prevent that, we cross one at a time, with every bag held tight to the body. The second hazard is the long descent: tiredness is the root cause of most falls, so we stop for ten minutes every hour and nobody walks at the back alone.

feedback.es: Una estufa fría indica que el grupo se fue hace horas: must have left hours earlier. No hubo accidente ni se habla de prisa.

origin.audio: A mountain volunteer describes a call-out. We found the tent open and the boots gone, she said. The stove was cold, so the people who had been there must have left hours earlier. There was no evidence of a fall or an injury, so it can't have been an accident; more likely the group had decided to move on before the weather changed. In hindsight, we had been worried about nothing.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud muestra ella al final de su relato?

feedback.es: «In hindsight, we had been worried about nothing» expresa alivio, aunque la alarma no llevara a nada.

feedback.es: Contributing factor es el factor que contribuye a un resultado sin ser su causa única.

origin.text: The report names no single person to blame. The late start at the bridge was a contributing ___ in the incident.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de una charla de riesgos para una excursión.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the preventive measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. If something goes wrong, we will look for the root cause, not for someone to blame. Are there any questions?

Hello, team. Today I want to explain two risks. The main hazard is the wind on the high ground. Strong gusts are highly likely, and the consequence could be a fall or another serious injury. origin.text: Vas a dirigir la charla de riesgos de una excursión de un día con una cresta y un río (entre 140 y 200 palabras). Presenta dos peligros con su probabilidad, su consecuencia y una medida de prevención (to prevent, unless, in case, had better).

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué postura adopta el guía ante el incidente?

choices.text: He believes the group did not take enough care.
He thinks the incident was unavoidable and no rule should change.
He wants lessons, not someone to blame.

feedback.es: Pide no culpar a nadie y aprender del incidente: busca lecciones, no culpables; descarta la falta de cuidado y dice que una medida sencilla lo habría evitado.

origin.audio: After the trip, the leader went over what had happened at the bridge. There was no evidence that anyone had ignored the rules, so he said it can't have been a lack of care. The delay might have been caused by the fog, and the injury must have happened when the rock moved under her foot. He asked the group not to blame anyone but to learn from it, because one simple preventive measure would have stopped it: crossing one at a time.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿con qué propósito lo escribe la organización?

choices.text: To justify a new rule without blaming any participant.
To admit that the organisers alone were to blame.
To ask participants to report similar incidents.

feedback.es: Explica una nueva medida tras el incidente y aclara que nadie tuvo la culpa: justifica la norma sin señalar a nadie.

origin.text: Dear participants, thank you for joining last Saturday's walk. Following the incident at the bridge, we have added a preventive measure to every briefing: all groups now cross one at a time. We do not believe anyone was at fault, but in hindsight the old routine was a contributing factor. We hope you will understand why the briefing is now a little longer.
